'''Ruth Signorell''' is a Swiss academic who works on fundamental [[Aerosol|aerosol science]]. In 2018 Signorell was awarded the [[Mildred Dresselhaus]] award, and in 2022 she was awarded the Doron Prize. She is a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|European Academy of Science]].

==Academic career==

Signorell studied mathematics at the [[University of Zurich]] and chemistry and physics at [[ETH Zurich]]. In 2012, Signorell was appointed as a full professor of physical chemistry within the Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences at ETH Zurich.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-02-23 |title=Doron Prize for Ruth Signorell |url=https://chab.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/d-chab-news/2022/02/doron-prize-for-ruth-signorell.html |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences |language=en |archive-date=3 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303093002/https://chab.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/d-chab-news/2022/02/doron-prize-for-ruth-signorell.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Signorell’s research focuses on fundamental aerosol science. She and her research group study the formation, physicochemical nature, structure and reactive processes of aerosols. In particular, Signorell is interested in new techniques for aerosol detection and in the behavior of nanoaerosols.<ref name=":1" /> She has led the development of models of the rate of chemical reactions in atmospheric droplets, and has studied the nucleation processes involved in the first microseconds of aerosol formation.<ref name=":0" /> Her work is relevant to environment processes in the atmosphere, as well as the behavior of aerosol particles in infectious diseases.<ref name=":0" />

Signorell is a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|European Academy of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ruth Signorell |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Signorell_Ruth |access-date=1 April 2025 |website=Academia Europaea: The Academy of Europe}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2018 Signorell was awarded the Mildred Dresselhaus Prize by the [[IEEE]] for “advancing the fundamental understanding of physical and chemical properties of aerosols and nanoparticles ubiquitous in our world”.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Mildred Dresselhaus Prize Recipients |url=https://www.cui-advanced.uni-hamburg.de/en/cluster/aktuelles/19-05-22-md-awardees.html |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=www.cui-advanced.uni-hamburg.de |language=en}}</ref> In 2020 she was made a member of the European Academy of Science, and was awarded a [[Humboldt Research Award]] “for her outstanding achievements in research and teaching”.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Swiss Chemical Society - Prof. Ruth Signorell, ETH Zurich, receives the Humboldt Award |url=https://scg.ch/scg-news/news-physical/prof-ruth-signorell-eth-zurich-receives-the-humboldt-award |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=scg.ch |archive-date=23 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723154152/https://scg.ch/scg-news/news-physical/prof-ruth-signorell-eth-zurich-receives-the-humboldt-award |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2022, she was awarded the Doron Prize.<ref name=":0" />
